analysis.file_name: BofA Who Makes the Data Center 2026 Primer 20261023.pdf
analysis.title: Who Makes the Data Center 2026 Primer
key_insights: BofA estimates global data center spending grew from $275bn in 2022 to nearly $1.0tr in 2026E and forecasts $2.1tr by 2028E, up 122% from the $939bn 2028 forecast in the 2025 edition.
The 2028E IT equipment forecast rose to $1,815bn from $792bn (+129%), with AI-related IT equipment at $1,496bn vs $629bn prior (+138%). Infrastructure spend rose 84% to $270bn from $147bn.
BofA forecasts a 37% market-wide CAGR over 2025-30E, reaching $2.9tr in 2030, driven by AI adoption. AI networking has the fastest CAGR at 63%, AI servers 50%.

The all-in cost of an average new-build US data center is $49mn per MW, up $10mn/MW from last year's edition. AI-focused builds cost $57mn per MW, and IT equipment drives $7mn of the $8mn increase. IT equipment is 78% of the total, electrical 5%, thermal 3%.
On a like-for-like basis, data center infrastructure costs are 10-15% higher y/y. Because of 18-24 month build times, much of the spending is already financed, permitted and contracted.
BofA estimates Schneider leads the $30bn electrical equipment market (24% share) and Vertiv leads the $18bn thermal market (17% share). The six largest electrical vendors hold nearly 80% share.

Neoclouds are forecast to own 6% of the energized data center market in 2026E, up from under 0.3% in 2023. US neocloud capex is forecast above $230bn by 2028. Most neocloud revenue is multi-year, fixed-rate contracts with hyperscalers and AI labs, and a smaller portion is exposed to GPU spot prices.
US cloud service provider capex is forecast above $1.2tr in 2028E. AWS generated $46bn of GAAP operating profit on $129bn of revenue in 2025 (35% margin).
Americas holds over half of global data center capacity. Capacity grew at a 24% CAGR over 2024-26E, with the Americas at 29%, EMEA 17% and Asia Pac 18%.

Nvidia's 'extreme codesign' and its one-year chip cadence favor infrastructure suppliers that offer integrated power and cooling and align with Nvidia's reference architecture. BofA says product-focused companies lacking complete systems offerings are likely to lose share.

Data center infrastructure M&A totals over $40bn since 2024. Examples include Eaton/Boyd Thermal at $9.5bn (22.5x EV/EBITDA), Madison Air/ebm-papst at $5.0bn, Ecolab/CoolIT at $4.75bn (29.0x EBITDA) and Flex/EPC Power at $4.4bn (13.1x EBITDA).

The shift to 400/800V direct current is driven by rack densities above 1,000kW. Initial deployments will use power sidecars, with first shipments expected in 2027. Content per MW is similar across architectures, but BofA considers its estimates likely conservative given silicon carbide components cost 5-10x more and an earlier ABB/Validus DC attempt had high initial costs.

Four companies have shipped solid-state transformers for data centers (Delta Electronics, ABB/Mitsubishi Heavy/DG Matrix, Eaton/Resilient Power, SIFANG). GE Vernova is in product validation with orders expected from 2027. Alternatives such as transformer rectifier units have more established supply chains but need more integration and footprint.

Modular and prefabricated products are gaining share because of labor bottlenecks. BofA sizes the 2026E modular market at $2.0-5.1bn gross, but only $0.5-1.8bn of true value-add (1-3% of electrical and thermal spend). Regal Rexnord received $0.7bn of E-pod orders in October 2025.

Direct-to-chip liquid cooling was roughly 15-20% of energized IT load in 2025 and could exceed 30% in 2026. Adoption is slower than investors expect but ultimate penetration may be higher. The liquid cooling market is $4-5bn in 2025 and likely to more than double in 2026. Eaton/Boyd and Vertiv each hold 17% share.

The industry is moving to dedicated IT cooling loops, separating a warmer liquid loop from the cooler air-cooling loop. BofA says investors overinterpret Jensen Huang's comment that Vera Rubin needs no water chillers, because facilities still need chillers for air-cooled equipment, even those 80-90% liquid cooled.

Air-cooled chillers are gaining on water-cooled for AI and colocation builds because of faster deployment and lower complexity, at the cost of efficiency. Water concerns are pushing a move to dry coolers and trim coolers. Absorption chillers could grow as on-site power generation grows.

BofA tracks 109 announced projects totaling 158 GW of on-site gas generation, of which about 2 GW is operating, 24 GW under construction, 36 GW probable, 25 GW possible and 71 GW speculative. Grid connection for new generation took a median of 5.1 years in 2025.
Wholesale colocation project economics assume $2.5mn per MW rent, 90% occupancy, 45% EBITDA margin and a 6.5% exit cap rate, giving a 10.7% IRR and $2.0mn NPV on $7mn equity. US occupancy is 96-97%.

Smaller market sizes (2025): UPS $12-16bn (Schneider 20%, Eaton 19%), switchgear $8-11bn (Schneider 31%), power distribution $8-11bn, chillers $4-6bn (JCI 23%), cooling towers $1.0-1.4bn (SPX 17%), air cooling $6-8bn (Vertiv 26%), generators $12-16bn (Caterpillar 42%), servers $415bn (ODM direct 52%, Dell 7%), networking $63bn (Arista 21%, Cisco 17%).
Top five hyperscalers are expected to grow capex 96% y/y in 2026 after 72% in 2025. The AI network fabric market is expected to grow to about $76bn by 2030 from $18bn in 2025.

sector_views.rationale: BofA raised its 2028E data center infrastructure spend to $270bn (+84%) and sees share gains for vendors with integrated power and cooling offerings aligned to Nvidia's architecture.
Neoclouds are forecast at 6% of energized capacity in 2026E, with US neocloud capex above $230bn by 2028 and revenue backed by multi-year contracts.

risk_factors: Neocloud risk: orchestration and GPU scheduling being open-sourced or brought in-house by customers, and full-stack AI platforms becoming more common.
Hyperscaler risk: AI training becoming distributed across regions.
Nvidia's one-year chip cadence can make infrastructure obsolete in about two years, and product-focused vendors lacking complete systems may lose share.
Direct current rollout risk from missing industry standards, technician training needs, and high initial costs of new components such as silicon carbide parts.
Liquid cooling adoption may be slower than investors expect, and two-phase cooling adoption remains limited by complexity and lack of standards.
Water consumption concerns and drought limit evaporative cooling, while dry coolers lose effectiveness in hot weather.
Grid connection delays (median 5.1 years) push developers to on-site power, which carries high capex and gas connection needs.
Speculative on-site power pipeline: 71 GW of the 158 GW announced has no start date or announced power developer.

Exhibit 7 shows global data center capacity of 91 GW in 2026E, up from 27 GW in 2019, with the Americas over 50% of the total.
Exhibit 5 shows electrical equipment market shares: Schneider 24%, Eaton 17%, Vertiv 12%, ABB 9%, Siemens 8%, Legrand 8%, others 22%.
Exhibit 6 shows thermal equipment market shares: Vertiv 17%, Johnson Controls 15%, Trane 7%, Stulz 6%, Carrier 5%, Modine 5%, Eaton 4%, Schneider 4%, others 37%.

tension_points.bull_case: Investors expect rapid liquid cooling adoption, with direct-to-chip reaching 15-20% of IT load in 2025 and possibly above 30% in 2026, and Jensen Huang said Vera Rubin's 45°C supply water needs no water chillers.
tension_points.bear_case: BofA says investors overinterpret this: chillers are still needed for air-cooled gear even in facilities 80-90% liquid cooled, and adoption is running slower than expected.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence that facilities can run without chillers for networking, power electronics and storage equipment would weaken the chiller demand case.

tension_points.bull_case: Neoclouds win on speed, specialization and utilization, with 18-24 month builds and multi-year contracts providing revenue visibility.
tension_points.bear_case: Revenue is concentrated in bare-metal compute for hyperscalers, and risk rises if orchestration and GPU scheduling is open-sourced or brought in-house.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Orchestration and GPU scheduling being open-sourced or brought in-house, or full-stack AI platforms becoming more common.

theme_stances.key_argument: Upward revisions to cloud capex, capital raising and construction starts support global data center spending of $2.1tr by 2028E.
theme_stances.evidence: Our current 2028 forecast is 122% higher than the 2025 edition

theme_stances.key_argument: Extreme codesign favors suppliers that offer both power and cooling and align with Nvidia's reference architecture.
theme_stances.evidence: Extreme codesign favors suppliers that offer both power and cooling capabilities.

theme_stances.key_argument: Higher liquid-loop temperatures reduce cooling needs but do not eliminate chillers, so investors overinterpret the no-chiller comment.
theme_stances.evidence: investors often overinterpret what this means for thermal infrastructure demand
